import { defineStyleConfig } from '@chakra-ui/react';

/**
 * Recipe — the cart drawer's Checkout / Apple Pay / Google Pay button stack (SFCC-275, SFCC-11
 * plan step 5.1). Single style, no parts: all three buttons get their full visual treatment from
 * `ZimmButton`'s own `primary`/`secondary` recipe (`zimmButton.css.ts`) — this recipe only owns
 * the group's own layout, matching `zimmCartItemActions.css.ts`'s single-style shape rather than
 * `zimmQuantityStepper.css.ts`'s multi-part one, since there is no second visual sub-part here to
 * name.
 *
 * `gap` is `var(--zimm-size-action-gap)` (16px) — session-notes.md §11.5 confirms Figma's
 * `gap-[16px]` is literally `space/400`, and `foundation/sizes.ts`'s own comment on `actionSizes`
 * confirms this is the SAME action-sizing token `ZimmButton`'s own `lg` size (h52/px32) already
 * resolves through, not a second, independently-typed 16px value.
 *
 * No fixed `height`/`minHeight` here, deliberately — SFCC-11 plan step 5.1 AC2 ("no white gap"
 * when the international variant renders one child instead of three): a plain flexbox `gap`
 * naturally removes both a removed child's own height AND its adjacent gap when that child is
 * gone, with nothing here to compensate. Adding a fixed height would silently reintroduce exactly
 * the dead-space bug AC2 exists to prevent — see this recipe's own `index.test.tsx` assertion
 * that no `height`/`minHeight` key exists on this baseStyle.
 */
export const ZimmCartButtonGroup = defineStyleConfig({
  baseStyle: {
    display: 'flex',
    flexDirection: 'column',
    width: '100%',
    gap: 'var(--zimm-size-action-gap)',
  },
});

Four things I found change the plan's shape — flagged inline where they land. --- # Cart bundle (SFCC-11) — executable build plan ---searching step 5.1--- 482:#### Step 5.1 — `ZimmCartButtonGroup` 486:**Real asset dimensions, confirmed 2026-09-21 when actually exporting them — the two logos are NOT the same aspect ratio, despite both being called "48×24" above.** `apple-pay-logo.svg` (`overrides/app/assets/svg/`) is natively `48×24` (viewBox `0 0 48 24`) — safe to render at `width={48} height={24}` directly, matches its own ratio exactly. `google-pay-logo.svg` is natively `45.1717×18` (viewBox `0 0 45.1717 18`) — Figma's own structure insets this smaller mark inside a nominal 48×24 slot, it doesn't fill one. **Both SVGs carry `preserveAspectRatio="none"` at the root**, so forcing the Google asset to `width={48} height={24}` directly will visibly stretch/distort the wordmark, not letterbox it. 579	## 5.0 Verification standard (added 2026-09-19, applies to every remaining step, 3.6 onward)
580	
581	Six real, currently-shipped defects were found in commits already scored PASS on Design fidelity,
582	by a from-scratch re-audit that rendered the real components live instead of reading source and
583	Figma side by side. Every one of the six traces back to one of the gaps below. These are now
584	mandatory for every remaining step's Design-fidelity check — not optional rigor, a gate. When
585	dispatching Tester/Scorer for 3.6 onward, brief them with this section explicitly: they start
586	each run with no memory of today, so the standard has to be restated, not assumed carried over.
587	
588	1. **A rendered-output claim needs a live measurement citation, not a source read.** "The recipe
589	   sets `fontWeight: 500`" is not the same claim as "the rendered text measures `font-weight: 500`
590	   in a real browser" — the first can be true while the second is false. Every Design-fidelity
591	   PASS from here on cites an actual measured value (computed style, bounding box, or a real
592	   screenshot) against the actual Figma-sourced value, for every property being signed off, not
593	   just the ones that seem most at-risk.
594	2. **A wrapper's correct style does not prove a nested element inherits it.** Two of the six
595	   defects were exactly this shape: `textStyle`/`fontWeight` correctly set on a container, silently
596	   lost before reaching the actual visible text, because the nested element was either a Chakra
597	   component with its own competing theme registration (`Heading`, and by extension `Button`/
598	   `IconButton`/`Modal`/anything imported from `@chakra-ui/react` un-wrapped in a plain `chakra.*`
599	   factory) or a literal HTML tag with its own default rendering (`<b>`, via a base SFCC
600	   component). Whenever a style is applied above a boundary like that, verify the leaf text node's
601	   own computed style directly — inheritance is not something to assume across it.

   a play function's own scripted end-state as a seeding bug.
5. **Read the real, current JSX before asserting how two elements relate.** More than one
   mis-scoped finding this pass came from reasoning about layout from a written description

237	// lg button: Handover action tokens confirmed by Figma auth drawer (node 40001855:28911) —
238	// 52px height, 32px padding X, 4px gap (--alias-space-100), 80px min-width.
239	// height/paddingX use foundation tokens; gap maps to --zimm-scale-2xs (4px).
240	// min-width has no --zimm-size-action-width-min token yet — provisional constant below.
241	//
242	// sm button: confirmed by Figma node 901:2897 — 40px height, 20px padding X. Both now
243	// use foundation tokens (action-height-md, action-padding-h-md) instead of raw values.
244	const BTN_MIN_WIDTH_LG = '80px'; // audit-allow: provisional — pending --zimm-size-action-width-min token
245	
246	// `textStyle` sets fontFamily/fontWeight/lineHeight/letterSpacing/textTransform via
247	// Chakra's expansion pass. BUT extendTheme deep-merges our sizes with Chakra's built-in
248	// Button sizes, and Chakra's default lg has `fontSize: 'lg'` (1.125rem = 18px) and sm
249	// has `fontSize: 'sm'` (0.875rem = 14px). Because direct CSS props applied after the
250	// textStyle expansion win in Chakra's style pipeline, the merged `fontSize` from Chakra's
251	// default overrides the textStyle-derived value. Fix: set `fontSize` explicitly here using
252	// the zimm CSS var so it overwrites the leaked default and the final rendered size matches
253	// typography.ts (button = 14px, buttonSm = 12px).
254	const sizes = {
255	  lg: {
256	    h: 'var(--zimm-size-action-height-lg)', // 52px — confirmed by Figma + Handover
257	    minW: BTN_MIN_WIDTH_LG, // 80px — Figma --alias-size-action-width-min, pending token
258	    px: 'var(--zimm-size-action-padding-h-lg)', // 32px — confirmed by Figma + Handover
259	    // fontSize / fontWeight / lineHeight explicitly set to override Chakra's deep-merged
260	    // Button.sizes.lg defaults (fontSize:'lg'=1.125rem, fontWeight:'semibold'=600,
261	    // lineHeight:'1.2') — same issue as the baseStyle fontWeight: these leak through
262	    // extendTheme's deep-merge even when textStyle sets the correct values.
263	    fontSize: 'var(--zimm-font-size-2xs)', // 14px
264	    fontWeight: 'var(--zimm-font-weight-medium)', // 500
265	    lineHeight: 'var(--zimm-font-lineheight-3xs)', // 16px
266	    textStyle: 'button',
267	  },
268	  sm: {
269	    h: 'var(--zimm-size-action-height-md)', // 40px — confirmed by Figma 901:2897
270	    px: 'var(--zimm-size-action-padding-h-md)', // 20px — confirmed by Figma 901:2897
271	    fontSize: 'var(--zimm-font-size-3xs)', // 12px
272	    fontWeight: 'var(--zimm-font-weight-medium)', // 500
273	    lineHeight: 'var(--zimm-font-lineheight-2xs)', // 18px
274	    textStyle: 'buttonSm',
275	  },
276	  // Social button responsive size. Figma confirms height/typography step at the md
277	  // breakpoint, but horizontal padding is 32px at every breakpoint — NOT responsive.
278	  // Corrected 2026-09: the previous version of this comment claimed padding also stepped
279	  // down to 20px on mobile ("Figma confirms all three variants"); live Figma inspection
280	  // showed that was wrong — px was always meant to be var(--zimm-size-action-padding-h-lg).
281	  // Mobile: 40px h, 32px px, buttonSm (12px/500/18px lh)
282	  // Desktop (md+): 52px h, 32px px, button (14px/500/16px lh)
283	  // Also used by primary/secondary buttons inside the auth drawer (size="adaptive")
284	  // via ZimmButton's adaptive→social size mapping — same tokens, different variant colours.
285	  social: {
286	    // h (explicit fixed height) guarantees the flex container has a known height so
287	    // align-items:center always has space to distribute. minH alone can resolve to nothing
288	    // if the CSS variable hasn't loaded, leaving the button at content height with no
289	    // centering space. whiteSpace:normal (from the social variant) still allows text wrapping
290	    // if the label needs it; overflow:clip (from baseStyle) handles any rare overflow.
291	    h: 'var(--zimm-size-action-height-md)',
292	    // Constant across breakpoints — see the comment above this size. Not var(--...-h-md)
293	    // (20px): that's the mobile action-height tier's own padding token, but this button's
294	    // horizontal padding was never meant to shrink with it.
295	    px: 'var(--zimm-size-action-padding-h-lg)',
296	    fontSize: 'var(--zimm-font-size-3xs)',
297	    fontWeight: 'var(--zimm-font-weight-medium)',
298	    lineHeight: 'var(--zimm-font-lineheight-2xs)',
299	    textStyle: 'buttonSm',
300	    [`@media (min-width: ${breakpoints.md})`]: {
301	      h: 'var(--zimm-size-action-height-lg)',
302	      fontSize: 'var(--zimm-font-size-2xs)',
303	      lineHeight: 'var(--zimm-font-lineheight-3xs)',
304	      textStyle: 'button',
305	    },
306	  },
307	  // WCAG 2.2 AA SC 2.5.8 — 24px minimum target size. SFCC-55's accessibility note names this
308	  // control specifically ("the minimum size of that email sign up button").
309	  //
310	  // minW/minH, NOT padding: Chakra's IconButton hard-sets `padding: "0"` as a *style prop*, and
311	  // style props merge after __css, so any p/px/py declared here is silently discarded. The
312	  // previous `p: 'xs'` read as a 32px target and rendered 16x16 — the icon's own boxSize.
313	  //
314	  // var, not 'xl': min-width/height resolve through theme.sizes (xl = 36rem = 576px), not
315	  // theme.space. Same rule and same token as clearButton in zimmTextInput.ts, which is the
316	  // sibling control in the same trailing slot.
317	  icon: {
318	    h: 'auto',
319	    minW: 'var(--zimm-scale-xl)',
320	    minH: 'var(--zimm-scale-xl)',
321	  },
322	};
323	
324	export const Button = defineStyleConfig({
325	  baseStyle,
326	  variants,
327	  sizes,
328	  defaultProps: {
329	    variant: 'primary',
330	    size: 'lg',
331	  },
332	});

335	// to strip Futura Round's metric whitespace above cap-height and below the alphabetic
336	// baseline so uppercase glyphs sit at the true visual centre.

338	  baseStyle: {
339	    flexShrink: 0,
340	    textBoxTrim: 'trim-both',
341	    textBoxEdge: 'cap alphabetic',
342	  },
343	});

1	/**
2	 * Zimmermann country configuration — combines SCAPI-derived site/locale/
3	 * currency truth (countries.generated.ts, regenerate via
4	 * `npm run sync:regional-config`) with a hand-maintained overlay for the
5	 * fields Business Manager/SCAPI has no concept of: shipping country,
6	 * checkout ownership, and boutique region grouping.
7	 *
8	 * Used by: URL routing, IP-detection prompt, checkout redirect logic,
9	 * boutique location filtering, hreflang generation.
10	 *
11	 * When adding a country:
12	 *   1. Add it to config/sites.overlay.js (and e2e/fixtures/site.overlay.js
13	 *      if it needs e2e coverage), then run `npm run sync:regional-config`.
14	 *   2. Add its business-logic overlay entry below (shippingCountry,
15	 *      checkoutOwner, globalEPricing, boutiqueRegion).
16	 *   3. Ensure a compiled translation exists in overrides/app/static/translations/compiled/.
17	 *
18	 * Unresolved — do not hard-code:
19	 *   - NZ/Oceania currency routing
20	 *   - Denmark routing
21	 *   - China
22	 */
23	
24	import { GENERATED_COUNTRIES } from './countries.generated';
25	
26	/**
27	 * Who owns checkout for this site's domestic path.
28	 * For HK and ME, Global-e always owns checkout AND pricing from PDP onward.
29	 * For AU, US, GB, EU: SFCC owns domestic paths; Global-e takes over when the
30	 * user's shipping destination is outside the site's domestic market.
31	 */
32	export type CheckoutOwner = 'sfcc' | 'global-e' | 'hybrid';
33

35	  /** URL path segment, e.g. 'au', 'us', 'fr-eu' */

37	  /** The real SFCC site this locale routes to */
38	  sfccSiteId: string;

40	  locale: string;
41	  /** ISO 4217 currency code */
42	  currency: string;
43	  /** ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 shipping/tax country */
44	  shippingCountry: string;
45	  /**
46	   * Checkout owner for this site's domestic path.
47	   * Branch checkout AND pricing logic from this field at PDP/cart level —
48	   * not only at the checkout page.
49	   */

51	  /**
52	   * When true, Global-e owns pricing, currency, and tax display from PDP
53	   * onward — do not render SFCC prices on these paths.
54	   */
55	  globalEPricing: boolean;
56	  /** Key used to filter boutique locations for this region */
57	  boutiqueRegion: string;
58	};
59	
60	type CountryOverlayEntry = Pick<
61	  CountryConfig,
62	  'shippingCountry' | 'checkoutOwner' | 'globalEPricing' | 'boutiqueRegion'
63	>;

input.prompt:
You are one of four parallel testers checking step 5.1 of the SFCC-11 Cart epic build, in repo /Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/Dev/zimmermann-pwa, branch feature/SFCC-11_cart (already checked out — do not switch branches, do not commit, read-only investigation only, do not edit any source file). This step added a new molecule `ZimmCartButtonGroup` (Checkout/Apple Pay/Google Pay button stack for the cart drawer footer) and extended the shared `ZimmButton` atom with a new `hideLabelVisually?: boolean` prop, which swaps a visible label `<span>` for Chakra's `VisuallyHidden` (an sr-only clip technique: `position:absolute; width:1px; height:1px; overflow:hidden`) — used so the Apple Pay/Google Pay buttons show ONLY their logo mark on screen while keeping the label text as a real (but visually clipped) DOM node for the accessible name.

YOUR LANE ONLY — three other testers own: tsc/vitest/audit:tokens/styling-conformance/mutation-testing; structure/imports/accessibility/DRY (static, not live); AC-by-AC ticket text + SVG byte-parity parsing + decision-log architecture claims. You own the ONE thing none of them can do: real, live-browser rendering verification. jsdom/Vitest cannot compute real flex layout, real bounding boxes, or real computed styles reliably for this — you must use an actual browser.

ENVIRONMENT: Storybook is already running at http://localhost:6006 (do not start a new instance). I already confirmed these exact story IDs are indexed and live:
- commerce-zimmcartbuttongroup--default
- commerce-zimmcartbuttongroup--international
- commerce-zimmcartbuttongroup--error-in-cart
Each story renders inside an iframe reachable directly at `http://localhost:6006/iframe.html?id=<story-id>&viewMode=story`. Playwright (`@playwright/test`, `playwright`) is already installed in node_modules with a cached Chromium build — you do NOT need to run `npx playwright install`. Write a plain Node script using the `playwright` package (not the test-runner, just `const {chromium} = require('playwright')` or ESM equivalent) and run it directly with `node`. Put any script files in the scratchpad directory given in your environment info — never in the repo itself.

Before writing your script, first read `overrides/app/components/ui-kits/molecules/zimmCartButtonGroup/index.tsx` and `zimmCartButtonGroup.css.ts` in full so you know exactly what you're trying to measure and why (component: chakra.div flex-col gap 16px containing up to 3 ZimmButton instances; Apple Pay/Google Pay wrap their logo in a fixed 48×24 `PayMarkSlot` span passed as `iconLeading`; Apple mark is natively 48×24 filling its slot exactly; Google mark is natively 45.1717×18, meant to render at its own real size CENTRED inside the same 48×24 slot, not stretched to fill it).

TASK 1 — All three stories render with no error boundary. Navigate to each of the 3 iframe URLs above, wait for network idle / the DOM to settle, and confirm: no React error boundary text, no "Something went wrong" / red screen, and the expected button count actually appears in the DOM (`#storybook-root button` — 3 for Default and ErrorInCart, 1 for International). Paste real counts.

TASK 2 — Icon-only fix, live confirmation (this is the single most important thing to verify — it was a previously-shipped defect, caught once already, now claimed fixed). On the Default story: locate the Apple Pay and Google Pay buttons. For EACH of their label text nodes (the text "Apple Pay" / "Google Pay" — NOT the SVG mark), get `getComputedStyle()` in the real browser and report the actual `position`, `width`, `height`, `overflow`/`clip`/`clip-path` values. Confirm they match the VisuallyHidden sr-only signature (`position: absolute`, `width: 1px`, `height: 1px`, `overflow: hidden` or equivalent clip). Do NOT use Playwright's `.isVisible()` or `.innerText()` to judge this — they will incorrectly report the text as visible/present regardless of the clip technique; you must read computed style directly via `page.evaluate`. ALSO take a real screenshot of the Default story (save to scratchpad) and visually describe what you see next to each mark — confirm there is no rendered "Apple Pay"/"Google Pay" caption text visible anywhere on screen next to the logo marks. Separately, confirm via `getComputedStyle` that the Checkout button's own label ("Checkout") is NOT clipped this way (`position` should not be `absolute` for that one) — it's supposed to stay genuinely visible.

TASK 3 — International story: confirm exactly 1 button in the DOM (already covered lightly in Task 1, but explicitly re-confirm `queryByRole`-equivalent: assert no element with accessible name matching /apple pay/i or /google pay/i exists anywhere in the rendered DOM, not just "not visible").

TASK 4 — AC2's "no compensating gap" height claim, LIVE MEASUREMENT (this is unverified by Vitest — the unit test only proves the recipe's baseStyle object has no hard-coded height/minHeight key, which is a source-read proxy, not a real measurement). On the Default story, get the real `getBoundingClientRect().height` of the button-group container (the outer `chakra.div` — you may need a stable selector; if there's no test-id, select by the element that has all 3 buttons as children, e.g. the common parent of the 3 `button` elements). Also get each individual button's real rendered height. On the International story, get the real height of the same container (now with 1 child). Compute: does `international_height ≈ default_height - (2 × single_button_height) - (2 × 16px_gap)`? Report the actual real numbers from both stories and state clearly whether the arithmetic holds (allow for sub-pixel rounding, but flag anything off by more than ~1-2px as a real discrepancy).

TASK 5 — Google Pay aspect-ratio / no-distortion, LIVE MEASUREMENT. Get the real `getBoundingClientRect()` of the actual innermost `<svg>` element for the Google Pay mark specifically (not its wrapping `<span>` or `<button>` — the task brief for this whole review explicitly warns that a container's correct position doesn't prove an inner element like an `<svg>` is itself correctly sized/centred, so measure the `<svg>` tag itself). Report its real rendered width/height and compute the ratio. Expected: ratio ≈ 45.1717/18 ≈ 2.51 (NOT stretched to 48/24 = 2.0). Do the same for the Apple Pay mark's `<svg>` (expected ratio ≈ 48/24 = 2.0 — it should fill its slot exactly since its native size already matches). If Google's rendered ratio comes out at ~2.0 instead of ~2.51, that is a real, confirmed distortion bug — report it prominently.

TASK 6 — Centring/alignment of the two marks. Still using the real `<svg>` bounding boxes from Task 5, compute each mark's vertical centre-line (top + height/2) relative to its own button's bounding box, and compare the two buttons' centre-lines to each other. The design claim (per this step's own code comments) is that both marks should align on the same visual centre line across the two buttons despite their different intrinsic sizes, because both sit inside an identical 48×24 wrapper slot. Report the actual real numbers and state whether they align (within ~1px).

TASK 7 — Focus-visible states, live spot-check. On the Default story, use real keyboard navigation (`page.keyboard.press('Tab')`) to focus each of the 3 buttons in turn and capture a screenshot or computed `outline`/`box-shadow` style for each when focused, vs. its own un-focused computed style. Confirm focus-visible is genuinely visually distinct from the resting state for all three (this is a live-rendering spot-check on top of what Vitest already asserts structurally from the recipe source — you're confirming the recipe actually paints as expected in a real browser, not re-deriving the recipe values).

TASK 8 — Story interactivity fidelity. Read `index.stories.tsx`'s three stories (Default/International/ErrorInCart) — none of them appear to expose Storybook args/controls (no `argTypes`, fixed decorators only, the component itself takes zero props). Confirm this by checking the live story's Controls panel is empty/non-interactive (or absent), and conclude explicitly whether this angle is applicable at all for this component (a component with zero props structurally cannot have a "picker/toggle that should change output" story gap — say so plainly rather than forcing a finding).

Report format: for each task, state the exact commands/script logic you ran and paste REAL numbers/output (not paraphrased). Label every finding CONFIRMED or PLAUSIBLE (you have a real browser, so most things here should be CONFIRMED one way or the other) and UNIFORM or ONE-OFF, with 🔴/🟡/🔵 severity. If Playwright or the Storybook connection fails for any reason, report the exact error and what you tried, rather than silently giving up on that task. End with what you could not verify and why. Keep your report self-contained and include the raw numeric measurements clearly (I need them to build a visual-checkpoint table) — I (the coordinator) will merge your report with three other testers' reports.
